title: How I redesigned my AI achievement guide viewer moving from a modal wall of text to a structured two-panel interface
author: Kmoyouknow
selftext:
I'm building AchieveIQ, an AI-powered Steam achievement guide generator. The guides are personalized to your actual save progress, not a generic walkthrough.

The first version of the guide viewer was a modal that dumped the full AI output as a wall of text. It worked but it wasn't usable. So I rebuilt it from scratch.

Here's what I changed and why:

\*\*The core problem:\*\* AI-generated guides are long. Elden Ring has 42 achievements, CK3 has 188. A single prose dump doesn't scale users couldn't find what they needed without reading the whole thing.

\*\*The solution: two panels:\*\*

Sidebar: Every achievement listed by difficulty (Easy, Medium, Hard, Missable) with collapsible sections. Completion icons pulled from Steam color for earned, greyed out for locked, green checkmark overlay on completed. Overall progress bar at the top.

Main panel: Three views

* Overview: playtime, projected hours to 100% at your current pace, per-difficulty breakdown with progress bars
* Achievement detail: click any sidebar item to see its difficulty badge, time estimate, missable flag, all extracted from the AI guide
* Full Guide: long-form prose, reads like a wiki. Sidebar clicks scroll directly to that achievement in the document

\*\*The streaming progress bar:\*\* Instead of a spinner during AI generation I estimate % complete based on guide length and stream a live progress bar. Small thing, massive perceived quality improvement.

\*\*The AI side:\*\* The structured sidebar data (difficulty groupings, time estimates, missable flags) is all extracted from the AI output. The prompt has to be precise enough that the model returns consistently parseable structure while still writing natural prose for the Full Guide view. Getting both right in a single generation pass was the interesting engineering problem.

Still early happy to talk through any of the decisions.

[achieveiq.vercel.app](http://achieveiq.vercel.app)
